text:
emma_support: heads-up — customer (ACME) is hitting intermittent 400s from embeddings endpoint. Error: \"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536 but got 1\". Started after they shipped a client patch. Sample resp: `{\"error\":\"dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1\"}`

sahil_client: they pasted the client code. looks like Node fetch: `await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' }, body: JSON.stringify({ input: JSON.stringify(embeddingArray) }) })` — ahhh they're JSON.stringify-ing the array twice so body.input becomes a string.

jon_prod: yep that would do it. server expects `input` to be an array (or list of strings). If you pass a single string that contains the array text, the runtime treats it as one input and the model returns a 1-d vector (or we error on validation). Repro snippet: 
```bash
# bad: sends a quoted string -> server sees single scalar
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"input":"[0.1,0.2,0.3]"}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings

# good: send array
curl -sS -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"input":[0.1,0.2,0.3]}' https://api.redwood.inference/v1/embeddings
```

emma_support: customer also mentioned it happens only during high throughput bursts. could there be a batching edge-case where we coerce types? headers from one failing request: `Content-Type: application/json`, `Content-Encoding: gzip`, client is urllib3 in Python (requests).

ryan_ml: two angles: 1) client double-stringifying OR 2) NDJSON/gzip boundary where a single-line string payload gets wrapped. If content-encoding is gzip + streaming, some clients will send lines without proper JSON framing. Can you grab a raw request body from logs (ingress) for one failing req_id? Also check whether they put `input` as a JSON-encoded string inside an array of inputs, e.g. `{"input":["[0.1,0.2]"]}` — that leads to embeddings for the whole string rather than vector input.

ops-bot: ingress: request_id=xyz-ff12 status=400 path=/v1/embeddings response_body=\"{\\\"error\\\":\\\"dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 1\\\"}\"\n

sahil_client: i reproduced locally — my library was `node-fetch` + I had a helper `serialize(payload) { return JSON.stringify(payload) }` and then did `body = JSON.stringify(serialize(obj))`. Fixed by removing the extra stringify. Patch rolling now.

emma_support: great catch. can we add a helpful validation message on our side? e.g. detect `input` that is a string starting with `[` and suggest the client unquote it. low effort mitigation to reduce escalations.

ryan_ml: we can add a quick heuristic in the validation layer: if `input` is a string and matches `^\s*\[.*\]\s*$` or `^\s*\{\"` then return 400 with a friendlier message: \"input appears to be a JSON-encoded string; send an actual array/object instead of a quoted string\". I'll file a small ticket and drop a canary.

emma_support: customer confirmed after patch they stopped seeing errors during burst test. closing thread after 24h of clean traffic. thanks all :tada:
